answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to anchor its identity to a costly, verifiable stake before it earns trust: instead of letting anyone plant a thousand fake agents like weeds in a garden, the network demands a deposit that is slashed when misbehavior is proven. A newcomer signs each claim with its own quill, so to speak, a unique key tied to that stake, and honest work slowly grows its reputation, while an attacker must pay the full deposit for every fake identity and lose it all when caught, making mass forgery unprofitable.
